snippet.title: Teleportation is real. #teleportation #quantumphysics #philosophy #science
snippet.description:
Teleportation is real. In 2017, a Chinese team teleported the quantum state of a single photon from the ground to a satellite up to 1,400 kilometres away, and the original was destroyed in the process.

It was not a person. The photon itself did not travel. Only its quantum state did, which is the full description of how it is set up. Think cut and paste, not copy and paste. And you cannot copy it first. The no-cloning theorem, shown in 1982 by William Wootters and Wojciech Zurek, and independently by Dennis Dieks, says you cannot perfectly copy an unknown quantum state. A state can be moved, never duplicated.

Then it gets personal. In his 1984 book Reasons and Persons, the philosopher Derek Parfit imagined a machine that scans you, destroys you, and rebuilds you on Mars. The person who steps out remembers everything you remember. Is that you, or did you die? And if the machine forgot to destroy the original, two people would remember being you.

Nobody is building this. A human body has about seven billion billion billion atoms, far beyond anything we can scan. But the question is real, because philosophers still disagree. Some say you are your memories and character. Others say you are your living body. Physics can tell you what happens to the particles. It cannot tell you whether that is a death or a delivery.

Honestly, I do not know which side I would pick. If a pod did it to you, would you step inside? Tell me in the comments.

Sources:

Ren et al., “Ground-to-satellite quantum teleportation”, Nature, 2017

Wootters and Zurek, “A single quantum cannot be cloned”, Nature, 1982

Dieks, “Communication by EPR devices”, Physics Letters A, 1982

Derek Parfit, Reasons and Persons, 1984

Wikipedia, “Composition of the human body” (atom count)

Stay curious!
